title: Je l'ai vu
intro: In the passé composé, object pronouns go **before the auxiliary** (**avoir** or **être**): *Tu as vu le film ? — Oui, je **l'ai** vu.* And when **la** or **les** comes before **avoir**, the participle agrees with it: *La valise ? Je l'ai pris**e**.*

cases.label: before the auxiliary
cases.rule: The pronoun goes **before the auxiliary**, never before the participle: *je **l'ai** vu, tu **m'as** appelé, il **lui a** parlé, je **les ai** invités*. **le** and **la** become **l'** before *ai, as, a, avons, avez, ont*.

cases.label: in the negative
cases.rule: **ne** + pronoun + auxiliary + **pas** + participle: *je **ne l'ai pas** vu, il **ne m'a pas** appelé, je **ne lui ai pas** répondu*.

cases.label: agreement with la, les
cases.rule: When a **direct object** pronoun comes before **avoir**, the participle agrees with it, like an adjective: *la tarte → je l'ai fait**e***, *les gâteaux → je les ai fait**s***, *les crêpes → je les ai fait**es***. The same goes for **me, te, nous, vous**: *Sophie, je t'ai attendu**e** !*

cases.label: no agreement with lui, leur
cases.rule: **lui** and **leur** replace **à** + a person: they are **indirect** objects, and the participle **never** agrees with them: *Sophie ? Je **lui** ai parlé* (not *parlée*). *Mes parents ? Je **leur** ai téléphoné.*

cases.label: en and y
cases.rule: **en** and **y** also go before the auxiliary: *Des crêpes ? J'**en** ai mangé trois. Marseille ? J'**y** suis allé.* The participle **doesn't agree** with **en**: *j'en ai mangé*, not *mangées*.

cases.label: agreement after que
cases.rule: **que** also puts the object **before** the verb, so the participle agrees with the noun it stands for: *la robe **que** j'ai achet**ée**, les photos **que** tu as pris**es***.

sections.title: 1. Before the auxiliary
text: In the passé composé, the verb has two parts: the auxiliary (**avoir** or **être**) and the participle. The pronoun goes **before the auxiliary**, the part that is conjugated.

examples.en: The film? I saw it yesterday.
Hugo? I called him this morning.

sections.tip: Never between the two parts: say *je l'ai vu*, not *j'ai le vu*. Before *ai, as, a…*, **le** and **la** become **l'**.

sections.title: 2. In the negative

head: Positive
Negative
rows: Je ne lui ai pas répondu.

examples.fr: Ton portable ? {Je ne l'ai pas vu|pcp-neg}.
examples.en: Your phone? I haven't seen it.

examples.fr: Hugo {ne m'a pas appelé|pcp-neg} hier soir.
examples.en: Hugo didn't call me last night.

sections.tip: The pronoun stays glued to the auxiliary: **ne** + pronoun + auxiliary + **pas** + participle.

sections.title: 3. Agreement with la, les
text: When **la, l'** or **les** stands for a **direct object** and comes before **avoir**, the participle agrees with it: **-e** for a feminine, **-s** for a plural, **-es** for both.

head: French
Agreement
rows: Les gâteaux ? Je les ai faits.
Les crêpes ? Je les ai faites.

examples.fr: Tes lunettes ? {Je les ai trouvées|pcp-accord} sous le canapé.
examples.en: Your glasses? I found them under the sofa.
Sophie, I waited an hour for you!

sections.tip: You can **hear** the agreement when the participle ends in a consonant: *pris → prise* /pʁiz/, *fait → faite* /fɛt/, *mis → mise*. With **-é**, you only see it: *trouvées* sounds like *trouvé*.

sections.title: 4. No agreement with lui, leur
text: **lui** and **leur** replace **à** + a person: they are **indirect** objects. The participle **never** agrees with them, even for a woman or a group.

head: With the noun
With the pronoun
rows: Tu as écrit à tes parents ?

examples.en: Your parents? Have you written to them?

sections.tip: Compare: *Sophie ? Je l'ai vue* (voir quelqu'un: direct, so it agrees) but *Sophie ? Je lui ai parlé* (parler **à** quelqu'un: indirect, no agreement).

sections.title: 5. en and y

head: Question
Answer
rows: Tu n'as pas pris de photos ?
Non, je n'en ai pas pris.

examples.fr: Le musée ? {Nous y sommes allés|pcp-en-y} dimanche.
examples.en: The museum? We went there on Sunday.

sections.tip: No agreement with **en**: *des crêpes → j'en ai mangé*, never *mangées*.

sections.title: 6. Agreement after que
text: **que** also puts the object **before** the verb, so the participle agrees with the noun that **que** stands for.

head: Sentence
With que
rows: C'est la robe que j'ai achetée.
Ce sont les photos que tu as prises.
C'est la lettre qu'il a écrite.
Ce sont les films que nous avons vus.

examples.fr: {La lettre que Jacques a écrite|pcp-que} est très drôle.
examples.en: The letter Jacques wrote is very funny.

examples.fr: Montre-moi {les photos que tu as prises|pcp-que} !
examples.en: Show me the photos you took!

sections.tip: The participle agrees only when the object comes **before** it. In *j'ai acheté une robe*, the object comes after: no agreement.

mistakes.why: The pronoun goes before **avoir**, not before the participle.
**l'** stands for *la valise*: the participle agrees (+ e).
After **que**, the participle agrees with the noun before it.

story.title: Tu l'as pris ?
story.en: A Saturday morning at Part-Dieu station: before the train to Marseille, Léa checks that Hugo hasn't forgotten anything.

lines.fr: Fin février, un samedi matin, à la gare de la Part-Dieu. Léa et Hugo prennent le train pour Marseille.
lines.en: At the end of February, on a Saturday morning, at Part-Dieu station. Léa and Hugo are taking the train to Marseille.

lines.fr: Le train part dans dix minutes. Léa vérifie tout, comme toujours.
lines.en: The train leaves in ten minutes. Léa checks everything, as always.

lines.fr: Les billets ? {Tu les as pris|pcp-place} ?
lines.en: The tickets? Have you got them?

lines.fr: Oui, {je les ai mis|pcp-place} dans mon sac.
lines.en: Yes, I put them in my bag.

lines.fr: Et ta carte d'identité ? {Tu l'as prise|pcp-accord} ?
lines.en: And your ID card? Have you got it?

lines.fr: Ma carte ? Euh… {je ne l'ai pas prise|pcp-neg}… Ah si ! {Je l'ai mise|pcp-accord} dans mon portefeuille.
lines.en: My card? Er… I haven't got it… Oh yes I have! I put it in my wallet.

lines.fr: Et ton portefeuille ? {Tu ne l'as pas perdu|pcp-neg}, cette fois ?
lines.en: And your wallet? You haven't lost it this time?

lines.fr: Non, regarde : {je l'ai gardé|pcp-place} dans ma poche !
lines.en: No, look: I've kept it in my pocket!

lines.fr: Tu as appelé Mamie ?
lines.en: Have you called Grandma?

lines.fr: Oui, {je lui ai téléphoné|pcp-coi} hier soir. Papi et elle nous attendent à la gare.
lines.en: Yes, I phoned her last night. She and Grandpa are meeting us at the station.

lines.fr: Et les fleurs pour Mamie ? {Tu les as achetées|pcp-accord} ?
lines.en: And the flowers for Grandma? Have you bought them?

lines.fr: Euh… non, {je ne les ai pas achetées|pcp-neg}. Mais j'ai des bugnes : {j'en ai acheté|pcp-en-y} une grande boîte !
lines.en: Er… no, I haven't bought them. But I've got bugnes: I bought a big box!

lines.fr: Hugo, il y a du sucre sur ton pull. {Tu en as mangé|pcp-en-y} combien ?
lines.en: Hugo, there's sugar on your jumper. How many have you eaten?

lines.fr: Seulement trois… ou six.
lines.en: Only three… or six.

lines.fr: Et tes lunettes ? {Tu les as oubliées|pcp-accord} ?
lines.en: And your glasses? Have you forgotten them?

lines.fr: Non… Mais où {est-ce que je les ai mises|pcp-accord} ?
lines.en: No… But where did I put them?

lines.fr: Sur ta tête, comme toujours !
lines.en: On your head, as always!

lines.fr: Dans le train, Léa montre des photos à Hugo.
lines.en: On the train, Léa shows Hugo some photos.

lines.fr: Regarde {les photos que j'ai prises|pcp-que} en août : Lou et toi, sur la plage de Marseille !
lines.en: Look at the photos I took in August: Lou and you, on the beach in Marseille!

lines.fr: Ah, Marseille… {On y est allés|pcp-en-y} tous les trois. Mamie nous a fait des crêpes tous les jours !
lines.en: Ah, Marseille… The three of us went there. Grandma made us crêpes every day!

lines.fr: À Marseille, Jacques et Louise les attendent sur le quai.
lines.en: In Marseille, Jacques and Louise are waiting for them on the platform.

lines.fr: Bonjour, mes chéris ! Hugo, {tu m'as apporté|pcp-place} des bugnes ?
lines.en: Hello, my darlings! Hugo, have you brought me some bugnes?

lines.fr: Oui, Mamie ! {Je les ai choisies|pcp-accord} pour toi.
lines.en: Yes, Grandma! I chose them for you.

lines.fr: Louise ouvre la boîte : il reste trois bugnes. Léa lève les yeux au ciel.
lines.en: Louise opens the box: there are three bugnes left. Léa rolls her eyes.

quiz.en: The film? I saw it yesterday.

quiz.q: “I called him.” Choose the right sentence:

quiz.en: Hugo? I saw him this morning.
Your phone? I haven't seen it.

quiz.q: “He didn't call me.” Choose the right sentence:

quiz.en: Your parents? Have you written to them?

quiz.q: Marseille ? J'___ suis allé en août.
quiz.en: Marseille? I went there in August.
Here are the photos I took.
